problem_motivation.content: It remains difficult to enhance strength without significantly reducing ductility in high-performance refractory alloys.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, it remains challenging to increase the strength of these alloys without seriously compromising their tensile ductility.

problem_motivation.content: The long-standing challenge of achieving alloys with both ultrahigh strength (>2 GPa) and sufficient ductility (>10%).
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, achieving alloys with an ultrahigh strength (>2 GPa) and a sufficient ductility (>10%) has presented a long-standing challenge.

prior_limitation.content: The strength-ductility trade-off remains difficult to solve in single principal-element alloy systems due to brittle W-enriched phases.
The stability of the high-temperature precipitate phase in nickel-base superalloys is a great challenge.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: but the stability of the high-temperature precipitate phase is still a great challenge

prior_limitation.content: Refractory HEAs with precipitation strengthening exhibit limited tensile ductility at ambient temperatures due to intrinsic brittleness of secondary phases.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Owing to the intrinsic brittleness of secondary phases that can form in these alloys, such as silicides, B2 and Laves phases, the majority of the previously reported refractory HEAs exhibit limited tensile ductility at ambient temperatures

prior_limitation.content: Single precipitation processes have limited potency for strengthening.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: With the single precipitation process though, the potency of the precipitation strengthening is still limited.

prior_limitation.content: Multiple precipitation sequences are difficult to control accurately because intermetallic compounds form at grain boundaries causing brittleness.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Instigating a sequence of multiple precipitations, however, is difficult to accurately control as intermetallic compounds can readily form at grain boundaries to result in material brittleness

causal_claim.content: The step I process with δ-lamella precipitation caused a significant hardening effect in the annealed alloy.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The high strength of this sample is testament to the fact that the designed alloy exhibits a high hardening effect during the step I process with δ-lamella precipitation.

causal_claim.content: Homogeneous distribution of SCCPs structure enables accommodation of many dislocations at coherent interfaces, preserving ductility.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A major reason for this is the homogeneous distribution of the SCCPs structure, which facilitates the steady accommodation of a large number of dislocations at the coherent δ/matrix interfaces during plastic deformation

mechanism_principle.content: The coherent interface between dislocations and delta lamellae reduces the likelihood of crack formation by causing shear misalignment instead of cleavage.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the coherent misalignment of δ-lamellae (Fig. 4c ) plays an important role in reducing the tendency for cleavage.

mechanism_principle.content: Small particle size and similar lattice parameter lower elastic interaction, preventing crack initiation at the interface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: because of the small size of the γ ″ particles and their similar lattice parameter to the fcc matrix, the associated elastic interaction between the γ ″ precipitates and cutting dislocations is correspondingly lowered [14] , [31] , [32] , [37] , thereby preventing any crack initiation at the precipitate–matrix interface during the deformation process.

hypothesis_statement.content: The proposed SCCP strategy, by facilitating dislocation transmission and relieving stress, will overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The coherent interfaces of SCCPs facilitate the dislocation transmission and relieve the stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation.

hypothesis_statement.content: Whether independently controllable multiple coherent precipitation structures can be tailored by stepwise thermo-mechanical processes to generate ultrahigh strength and ductile refractory HEAs.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Accordingly, the question that arises is whether independently controllable multiple coherent precipitation structures can be tailored by stepwise thermo-mechanical processes to generate ultrahigh strength and ductile refractory HEAs.

hypothesis_statement.content: The proposed study aims to develop a tungsten-based refractory HEA with a dual-phase structure to achieve ultra-high strength and ductility at ambient and elevated temperatures.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this work, we utilize the immense compositional space of multiple-principal-element alloys to develop a promising tungsten-based refractory HEA with a dual-phase structure.

evidence_result.content: The developed alloy achieved specific ultrahigh strength and ductility values at room temperature and high temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: our alloy displays an ultrahigh strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature, with a high yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C.

evidence_result.content: High-density dislocation walls form due to heavy cold-rolling, creating a structural basis for precipitation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Based on the heavy cold-rolled process, the dislocation density in the material increases sharply (Fig. 1d ), forming high-density dislocation walls (Fig. 1g )

evidence_result.content: Coherent δ nano-lamellae appear rapidly during initial annealing at 900 °C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Coherent δ nano-lamellae appeared rapidly during the initial stage of annealing at 900 °C (Fig. 1h and Supplementary Fig. 3a )

evidence_result.content: Grain size stabilizes below 1 μm due to dispersion of the stable δ phase during recrystallization.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the grain size eventually stabilized at below 1 μm due to a dispersion of the stable δ phase (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Fig. 3c )

evidence_result.content: High-density γ″ particles form with an ordered D022 structure after aging at 650°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: After aging at 650°C, nano-granular γ ″ phases formed successively. The morphology and ordered D0 22 structure of the high density γ ″ particles were revealed by dark-field (DF) TEM imaging (Fig. 1i )

evidence_result.content: The γ″ unit cell's ellipsoid shape is attributed to high elastic distortion energy in the [001] direction due to an axial ratio close to 2.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The axial ratio of the γ ″ unit cell is very close to 2, so its ellipsoid shape can be ascribed to the high elastic distortion energy in the [001] direction.

evidence_result.content: APT confirms both δ and γ″ precipitates have a composition of (Ni70Fe5)3(Ta20W5) despite different morphologies.
evidence_result.evidence_span: From the proximity histograms, the composition of the δ and γ ″ precipitates were both identified as (Ni 70 Fe 5 ) 3 (Ta 20 W 5 )

evidence_result.content: Tensile uniform elongation increased to ~15% while yield strength reached 2.0 GPa after Step II (γ″ strengthening).
evidence_result.evidence_span: With the subsequent γ ″ -strengthen (Step II), the yield strength of the material can be further increased to 2.0 GPa with an ultimate tensile strength of 2.15 GPa without compromising the tensile ductility, which actually increases to ~15%.

evidence_result.content: A yield strength above 1 GPa is maintained at temperatures up to 800 °C, attributed to sluggish grain growth.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, a yield strength above 1 GPa is maintained at temperatures as high as 800 °C due to sluggish grain growth (Supplementary Fig. 12 )

evidence_result.content: Quantitative measurement of hardening contribution from gamma double prime precipitates via tensile testing.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The hardening from the γ′′ can be measured by uniaxial tensile testing to be ~600 MPa (Fig. 3a )

evidence_result.content: Measured uniform elongation demonstrating retained ductility.
evidence_result.evidence_span: which we measured as a uniform elongation of 15%

constraint.content: APT samples were examined at a specific low temperature to ensure valid voltage mode operation.
constraint.evidence_span: These APT samples were examined at 50 K in voltage mode.

constraint.content: A specific strain rate was required for the room temperature tensile tests.
constraint.evidence_span: uniaxial tensile tests were carried out at room temperature at a constant strain rate of 5 × 10 −4 s −1

constraint.content: A different specific strain rate was required for the high-temperature tensile tests.
constraint.evidence_span: High-temperature tensile tests were conducted on the same MTS-810 testing machine at a strain rate of 10 −3 s −1

contradiction.content: In contrast to traditional alloys where dislocation pile-ups cause microcracks, this alloy's coherent interface prevents crack initiation.
contradiction.evidence_span: Unlike traditional W-based heavy alloys where intermetallic compounds invariably act as the origin of microcracks from major dislocation pile-ups during deformation, the coherent interface of the δ phase in the W-based HEA effectively alleviates this problem
